title: Add an easy-grip zipper loop
instruction: Feed the loop through the slider tab, cinch it, then use it to pull the zipper closed.
context: An attached cord loop makes a small zipper pull easier to grasp. Closing the zipper tests that the loop carries load.
setup: Two YAM arms face a 380 × 354 mm rubber work mat. A short textile garment panel is laid flat with its metal zipper partly open. Its slider has an 18 mm diameter pull eye and 90 mm available closing travel. A soft orange cord loop about 7 mm thick is staged beside the slider, with its leading bight to the left and its tail to the right.
scoring: 0.33 for feeding the bight through the eye by over 31 mm. 0.67 for forming the hitch with both bight and tail advances over 24 mm. Award 1.00 when pulling the added loop moves the slider more than 83 mm toward closed and it holds there for 0.55 s after release.
reset_notes: Open the slider to its start mark and remove and restage the loop beside the pull eye.
fidelity: The bight and tail use guided motions. A coupled force acts on the slider only after measured threading and cinching. The cord is rendered as a deforming curve rather than a full rope-contact solve.
scores: Scripted dual-YAM: 1.00 in 280 actions. Dream-1: 0.00 in 1,200 actions.
